## Available development release

[**v0.4.0-preview.6**](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.6)
provides checked Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.35+) and Windows x86-64 binaries.
No Rust compilation is needed. [Install that explicit version](install.qmd);
GitHub's stable Latest remains the older v0.3.0.

This development prerelease includes local builds, inspectable build records,
readable backup histories and verified recovery of saved local folders.
The table summarizes supported Rust CLI behavior; it does not establish R/IDE parity. See the
[detailed status](preview-status.qmd) and [delivery evidence](release-delivery.qmd)
for exact verification and limits. Newer changes on main need their own evidence.

| Capability | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| Choose the project | `--project PATH` selects the folder for a command. Child queries retain that root. |
| Preview an analysis | `build-dev` runs your selected steps without CLI version changes, copying preview results to final folders or uploading backups. |
| Read without changing files | Configuration validation and path queries do not create target folders or edit ignore files. |
| Detect command failures | Errors produce a nonzero exit status, so an automated run can stop. |
| Run without questions | `--non-interactive` disables CLI prompts and automatic package installation, and closes runner input. |
| Select no analysis | An explicit `scripts: []` runs no analysis scripts. Hooks may still run; production can export existing outputs. |
| Run scripts and render documents | The build engine supports Python, R, Quarto and R Markdown/Bookdown targets, with the corresponding tools installed. |
| Keep a local output archive | Production builds can export configured outputs to local content-addressed storage, which avoids storing identical content repeatedly. |

### Preview has a boundary

The CLI skips its own release operations during a preview, including cleanup
of released outputs and prior caches. **This is not a filesystem sandbox.**
Scripts, hooks and renderers can still change files. Queries for generated results point to the chosen temporary folder for that version. Use those
paths from your scripts, as in the [tutorial](tutorial.qmd); arbitrary writes are
still outside that rule.

Document renderers have their own working folders and output rules.
Mixed-language scheduling is not a promise that every target runs in the exact
order written in configuration. See the [build reference](cli/build.qmd) for
the current implementation and the [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) for limits.

## Known limits of the published preview

- A preview is not a filesystem sandbox. Scripts and hooks control their writes;
  automatic redirection of every renderer's output is not provided.
- Matching results and paths across CLI runs, RStudio and GUI rendering has not
  been proved.
- Complete compatibility with every `projr` workflow has not been established.
- Mixed script and document targets do not have a complete sequential-order
  guarantee.
- This preview supplies only Linux and Windows x86-64 binaries; macOS and ARM
  delivery are unavailable.
- Production recovery is bounded. It does not undo arbitrary script writes or
  partial external publication effects.

The existing projr R package is unchanged. The new source package projcli is
available in this repository: see its [installation and quick start](r-frontend.qmd)
and [function reference](r-reference.qmd). It is not on CRAN; preview.6 includes
the supported M4 CLI subset and optional R maintenance. Python/Julia frontends and complete R/IDE parity remain
separate work.

## Added in preview.5

Use the separate [R package](r-frontend.qmd) for supported build, path and
configuration functions. Optional production actions can generate documentation,
render README.Rmd and snapshot renv dependencies; they default off.

[Complete CAS stores on GitHub](cas-github.qmd) share identical files inside one
store. [Experimental Xet](xet-storage.qmd) shares pieces of files locally and uses
the same local engine through GitHub ZIPs. Both GitHub options transfer the whole
store, keep old immutable exports, and need trusted project records identifying the saved ZIPs for restore.
Xet's helper is separate and qualified on Linux/WSL; native Windows Xet is unsupported.

The [real synthetic round-trip](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/40510154990)
uploaded two versions per structure and restored both into fresh projects.
This is bounded test evidence, not whole-projr parity or a dataset savings promise.

## Planned work

M2 build records and the agreed M3 local recovery scope are included. Full
environment reproduction, automatic snapshot discovery and analysis-free
publication retry remain separate work. General command/argv steps and stronger execution policies
remain follow-ups; they are not silently interpreted from missing script paths.

For the detailed evidence, scope and decisions, see the
[behavior contract](behavior.qmd) and [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd).

## Included in preview.2

The released CLI keeps a captured project context, defaults generated-output
queries to a safe versioned cache, and uses native working folders unless you
choose the project-folder override. It supports explicit R-package data management,
none/pre/post output cleanup, success-only output promotion and local archives.
Supported HTML defaults to embedded resources only when no effective embedding
option was supplied; explicit and inherited false remain respected.

Real acceptance covers configured/no-init and fresh directory initialization,
ordered Python/R/report steps, a computed CSV and embedded report, structured
failures and verified final/archive bytes without Git credentials. See
[the acceptance and delivery evidence](release-delivery.qmd).

Bookdown site embedding is unchanged. Existing R helpers and R/IDE parity, linked
HTML portability, complete provenance and publication retry remain outside this
claim. The [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) remains the detailed source of scope.

Preview.3 includes [projr-compatible production CSV inventories](storage-design.qmd#compatible-csv-inventory),
independent of CAS.


## Remote work in preview.3

Preview.3 can upload selected outputs to ordinary local folders or GitHub
Releases, keep versioned snapshots and restore files. It supports comparison by
files or recorded history, with explicit controls for what gets uploaded.

A small synthetic project has completed a real GitHub upload, replacement and
restore sequence, including reuse of an unchanged archive and preservation of
older snapshots. See the [remote verification](remote-compatibility.qmd#live-github-fixture-verification)
and [command reference](cli/remote.qmd) for the tested scope and limits.

These ordinary remote additions were introduced in preview.3 and remain in
preview.4. The separate test prerelease holds sample data, not an installer. Complete projr
compatibility remains unproved. Preview.4 adds the named locations and file
histories below.

## Choose where a build saves its results

In preview.4, name each available storage destination once under
remotes, then select where this build sends its results with build.dest. A named
location remains available for restoring earlier data after you stop uploading
to it. The [configuration reference](configuration.qmd) has copyable examples
and explains how to select only particular folders.

For local content-addressed storage (CAS), identical file bytes are stored once
and folders receive fingerprints based on their names and contents. The new
tree writer can keep the complete folder listing in the storage location, in
your project, or in both. It always keeps a small project record identifying
the saved folders. That small record alone cannot restore files if the storage
content or required full listings are lost.

These additions are included in preview.4. Automatic version selection for CAS restore remains deferred; local CAS CSV/JSON history is described below. Explicit named-ID tree recovery is described below. Ordinary local and GitHub Release upload/restore behavior
remains available as described in the [remote guide](remote-compatibility.qmd).

## Check and recover a saved folder

In preview.4, you can check the exact file bytes in a local tree
snapshot, then restore a selected folder. Choose its configured storage name and
snapshot ID explicitly; this first command slice does not find a version for you.
The [remote reference](cli/remote.qmd#verify-or-restore-an-exact-local-cas-tree-snapshot-development-source)
shows both commands.

Restoring an older folder still works after you stop uploading that folder.
A complete snapshot saved remotely can recover files into a fresh configured
project. The command leaves your project version and stored snapshot unchanged.
It checks the data before replacing files; choose --clear only when you want to
remove destination-only files as well. This is included in preview.4.


Existing flat CAS snapshots can also be checked and restored by exact ID without
converting them. See the [remote reference](cli/remote.qmd#recover-existing-flat-cas-snapshots).
Their older file lists do not record empty folders, so those cannot be restored
from that format. Local CAS CSV/JSON history is described below; ordinary/GitHub flat publication is also implemented below; Ordinary local and GitHub tree metadata are described below.

## Keep a readable history of saved files

In preview.4, a local store can keep a CSV history you can filter in
Excel, or a JSON history you can open as text. When a folder has not changed,
a later version points directly to its earlier complete listing. Changed versions
still list every current file. The [configuration example](configuration.qmd#flat-history-in-local-cas)
shows how to choose the format and where to keep the full history.

You can optionally shorten repeated hashes using a file dictionary. That adds
indirection, so it is off by default. File-byte storage already avoids duplicate
content independently of these choices. The existing project manifest.csv remains
unchanged. These additions are included in preview.4.


## See which files reached a local backup

In preview.4, local folder backups can keep readable CSV or JSON lists
for each build. The list describes files actually stored, including older files
your upload settings deliberately keep. An unchanged folder points to its earlier
complete listing. CSV stays suitable for filtering in Excel: a reference row tells
you which earlier version to filter.

For archived backups, the record also tells you which physical version folder
contains the bytes. Keeping the latest folder replaces its older contents; a
historical list does not recreate bytes that have since been overwritten.
See [the configuration example](configuration.qmd#ordinary-local-flat-history).
This addition is included in preview.4.


## Keep a readable file history with GitHub backups

In preview.4, GitHub backups can also keep CSV or JSON file lists.
Choose which folders to upload, save a complete listing in the project, on GitHub,
or both, and retain a small project record pointing to the saved files.
An unchanged folder can point to an earlier complete listing. Optional formats
can reduce repeated file information while retaining every filename.

The list describes the ZIP actually prepared for upload. If an archived folder
is reused, its record names that older ZIP. A failed upload keeps the local
release and reports that some files may already have been sent. The tool avoids
replacing a history bundle that another writer changed while the build ran.
See [the copyable example and limits](configuration.qmd#github-flat-history).
This addition is included in preview.4. HTTP transport tests use
synthetic local servers; they are not a new live GitHub round-trip claim.


## Keep folder fingerprints with local backups

Preview.4 can give each saved folder a code based on its filenames and
contents. Unchanged subfolders keep the same codes across builds. Backups retain
their normal versioned folders, and a readable JSON history still shows the
complete file lists or points to the earlier unchanged listing.

Choose tree style in [this local-backup example](configuration.qmd#ordinary-local-tree-history).
The small project record keeps the folder code even when complete metadata stays
with the backup. This addition is included in preview.4.

## Keep folder fingerprints with GitHub backups {#github-tree-backups}

GitHub backups normally keep a flat file list. You can also save fingerprints
for each folder and its children, while keeping the same downloadable data ZIPs.
Set manifest-style: tree on that remote; the
[configuration reference](configuration.qmd#github-tree-history) gives a complete
example and explains where the listings are saved.

The saved file list describes what actually reached the ZIP, including retained
older files when your upload settings request them. Identical folder contents
have the same fingerprint across versions. A small project record identifies
the saved root even when full listings live on GitHub. Earlier flat records
remain readable when you change this setting. This feature is included in preview.4.

## Added in preview.6

- Create project metadata from the CLI or named R helpers, with optional
  DESCRIPTION, README.Rmd, citation metadata and renv initialization.
- Keep an existing DESCRIPTION Version synchronized with VERSION by default.
- Select named script directories or globs, with exclusions and stable ordering.
- Put grouped reports under the configured docs folder and retain complete
  Quarto website output trees.

Separate reports copy their output and generated `<stem>_files` folder. When
embedding is explicitly disabled, authored assets elsewhere are not collected
automatically. Use embedded HTML or a Quarto project for portable output.
